title: cost-heuristic-playbooks-batch-cache-quant-presets
author: Asha Nambiar
description: Summary: Add a rule-driven "playbooks" subsystem that emits conservative batching, KV-prefix caching, and quantization preset recommendations by workload class. Motivation: customers running mixed workloads need predictable unit economics without manual tuning. This PR introduces an opinionated, auditable layer of heuristics (playbooks) that map runtime signals and profile metadata to safe defaults and rollout suggestions. Design notes: playbooks are authored as ordered rule sets (YAML) evaluated at request-time and as an offline batch to generate recommendations for Console and the Optimize service. Rules evaluate inputs: model family, sequence length distribution, p50/p95 latency SLO, token cost targets, and observed cache hit rates. Each rule yields a scored action bundle: {batch_size, cache_ttl_ms, kv_cache_mode, quant_profile}. A conservative scoring function biases toward smaller batch sizes for low-SLO, larger batching for background jobs, and prefers per-model quant profiles only when eval regressions are below threshold. Backwards compatibility: runtime falls back to existing default pipeline if playbooks return no action. Playbooks are namespaced by customer and can be disabled with a runtime flag (ENABLE_COST_PLAYBOOKS=false) for private deployments. Changes include: 1) a small rule engine and serializer, 2) a set of initial playbooks tuned for conversational, completion, and embedding workloads, 3) UI surfaces in Console (recommendation cards + accept/apply flow), 4) telemetry hooks for A/B and unit-econ tracking, 5) e2e and unit tests and benchmark harness. Testing & results: Microbenchmarks (internal perf-canary profiles) show median token cost reduction 12-18% on conversational workloads with <=2% increase in p99 latency; background batch workloads see 20-26% unit-cost reductions with no latency SLO degradation. We ran a canary across 5 dedicated pods (mixed traffic) for 72 hours; seen stable cache hit improvement and no elevated error rates. Checklist: - [x] rule engine + serializer - [x] initial playbook YAMLs for 3 workload classes - [x] Console UI + apply flow - [x] telemetry and tracing hooks - [x] unit/e2e tests and benchmarks - [x] rollout/canary plan and rollback flag Rollout plan: start with opt-in for Dedicated customers, run for 1 week on canary fleet, measure cost/eval regressions, then progressive enable with Linear ticket gating. Related tickets: ENG-1345, ENG-1378. Notes: quant presets are conservative by design (prefer per-model 8-bit configs that passed eval ramp), and all changes are reversible. For emergency rollback set ENABLE_COST_PLAYBOOKS=false and clear playbook cache across backends.
